Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

bias noun

also biased, partiality, partial (biased), partisanship, prejudice, prejudiced, preconception, unbiased, without bias

classical

Tac. Ann. 1.1: sine īrā et studiō

studium, studiī n.

noun, second declension

bias, partisanship, favour for one side

Its ordinary senses are zeal, eagerness, interest and study; as bias it is the eagerness that takes a side, studium partium, party spirit (Cic. Verr. 2.1.35, Lewis & Short). Tacitus promises to write sine īrā et studiō, without anger and without bias.

Other words

  • opīniō praejūdicāta, opīniōnis praejūdicātae f. — preconception, prejudice

    also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.10 (Lewis & Short, s.v. praejūdicō); M-O s.v. bias: preconceived notion

    An opinion formed before the facts are heard. nē quid praejūdicātī afferātis, “bring no prejudice with you” (Cic. Clu. 6).

  • cupidus, cupida, cupidum — biased, partial (of a judge or witness)

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Font. 21: cupidī et īrātī et conjūrātī testēs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Caecin. 8: cupidior jūdex (Lewis & Short)

    Its ordinary sense is eager, desirous (see want); of a judge, a witness or an author, partial, inclined to one side. The adverb cupidē is “with bias” (M-O s.v. bias).

  • praejūdicium, praejūdiciī n. — a prior judgment, a precedent

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 12; Quint. 5.2.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Classically a judgment given beforehand, a precedent, not a prejudice of the mind; the sense of harm to a case is legal and later. For prejudice, opīniō praejūdicāta.

Examples

  • sine īrā et studiō, quōrum causās procul habeō

    without anger or bias, whose causes I am far removed fromTac. Ann. 1.1

  • postulō, ut nē quid hūc praejūdicātī afferātis

    I ask you not to bring any preconceived opinion with you hereCic. Clu. 6 (Lewis & Short)

See also opinion, justice, reasonable.
